title: The counterexample that can't happen
objective: Given a satisfiable inductive step, decide whether the invariant is inductive, needs strengthening, or is reachable and needs a fix, using a bounded search that prints its bound; then strengthen it until all three checks hold and choose the claim your evidence supports.

blocks.md:
Z3 has just handed you a state. It satisfies your invariant, a command can run from it, and the next state breaks the invariant. Your instinct is to fix the command. Of the three things that state can mean, only one calls for that.

This lesson is about telling them apart with a search from `Init`, and about what you may claim when the search and the strengthening both fall short.

choice.prompt: The inductive step for `bal ≥ 0` on the holds model comes back with a pre-state where `bal = 0` and `held = 1`. A `Capture` of 1 from there leaves `bal = −1`. What do you do next?

options.text: Fix `Capture`, because it lets a balance go negative.
options.why: A bug needs a run from `Init` that reaches that pre-state, and nobody has looked for one. A failing step from a state you cannot reach is no evidence against the command.

options.text: Ask whether `held > bal` is reachable from `Init`, and if it is not, strengthen the invariant.
options.why: A counterexample to induction is a bug only when its pre-state is reachable. Reachable means fix the command. Unreachable means the invariant forgot a fact.

options.text: Report that the property is false, because the solver found a violation.
options.why: The query starts from any state with `bal ≥ 0`, not from `Init`. Its model is a step that could break the invariant, not a run that does.

options.text: Ignore it, because the pre-state is only hypothetical.
options.why: Dismissing it skips the one check that can turn it into a real bug: whether any run reaches that state.

choice.prompt: A bounded search from `Init` finds no violation within 6 steps. What may the claim carry?

options.text: PROVED [P] for every run.
options.why: Six steps say nothing about step seven. Only an inductive step with no counterexample covers every run.

options.text: MODEL-CHECKED [M] · bound 6 · partial.
options.why: A bounded search earns [M] with its bound printed, and "partial" because deeper runs were never searched.

options.text: TESTED [T] · n = 6.
options.why: Six is a depth, not a sample count. The search covers every run of up to six steps, not six chosen ones.

options.text: REFUTED [R] · 6 steps.
options.why: Nothing was found, so nothing is refuted. [R] needs a trace that replays.

blocks.md:
The holds model from S4.L4 has one account and three commands. `Hold(n)` sets `n` aside, `Capture(n)` spends held funds, and `Release(n)` frees them. The invariant is `bal ≥ 0`, and its inductive step query returns a pre-state in which `held` exceeds `bal`. One `Capture` from there pushes `bal` below zero.

That state is a counterexample to induction, a CTI: it satisfies the invariant, a step is enabled, and the invariant is broken one step later. A CTI says nothing about whether any run reaches the state. The step query starts from any state that satisfies the invariant, reachable or not.

So a satisfiable step query leaves one more question: can a run from `Init` reach the pre-state? Ask Z3 for a run of k steps from `Init` that ends with the invariant broken, for k = 0, 1, 2 and on up to a bound N that you choose and print. The first k that has a model is a trace. Replayed in the interpreter, it becomes REFUTED [R] with its length. If no k does, all you know is that there is no violation within N steps.

| Step query | Search from `Init`, up to N | Verdict | What you do |
|---|---|---|---|
| no model | not needed | inductive | check `Init ⇒ Inv` and `Inv ⇒ Safe`, then mint CL-4.4 |
| a model | a trace at step k | reachable | fix the command; the stamp is REFUTED [R] with k steps |
| a model | nothing within N | CTI so far | strengthen the invariant; if that stalls, mint CL-4.5 |

The last row says "so far" on purpose. Nothing within N is silent about runs longer than N, so the search cannot prove a pre-state unreachable. A CTI verdict becomes firm only when your strengthened invariant passes every check, which is the next segment.

Here are two models. The good model's `Hold(n)` requires `n ≤ bal − held`. Its twin's `Hold(n)` requires only `n ≤ bal`, and forgets holds already placed. Both give the same shape of CTI. Call the twin before you run anything.
The inductive step and a bounded search, on the twin and then on the good model.
blocks.direction: Query asserts: first, a state with `bal ≥ 0`, one step of the model, and `bal < 0` afterwards. Then, for each k up to the bound, a run of k steps from `Init` that ends with `bal < 0`. `sat` on the step query means a CTI exists. `sat` on a search query means a real run breaks the invariant.

code.text:
from z3 import *

def explore(name, hold_guard, bound=6):
    # One step of the holds model, from (bal, held) to (bal2, held2).
    def step(s, t, n):
        (bal, held), (bal2, held2) = s, t
        return And(n > 0, Or(
            And(hold_guard(bal, held, n), held2 == held + n, bal2 == bal),   # Hold(n)
            And(n <= held, held2 == held - n, bal2 == bal - n),              # Capture(n)
            And(n <= held, held2 == held - n, bal2 == bal)))                 # Release(n)

    # The inductive step for bal >= 0: a state with bal >= 0, one step, then bal < 0.
    bal, held, bal2, held2, n = Ints('bal held bal2 held2 n')
    q = Solver()
    q.add(bal >= 0, step((bal, held), (bal2, held2), n), bal2 < 0)
    print(name, '- inductive step:', q.check())
    m = q.model()
    print('  held > bal in the pre-state:', m[held].as_long() > m[bal].as_long())

    # Bounded search from Init: a run of k steps that ends with bal < 0.
    for k in range(bound + 1):
        s = [(Int(f'bal{i}'), Int(f'held{i}')) for i in range(k + 1)]
        search = Solver()
        search.add(s[0][0] >= 0, s[0][1] == 0)                  # Init
        for i in range(k):
            search.add(step(s[i], s[i + 1], Int(f'n{i}')))
        search.add(s[k][0] < 0)                                  # the invariant fails at step k
        if search.check() == sat:
            m = search.model()
            ops = []
            for i in range(k):
                h0, h1 = m[s[i][1]].as_long(), m[s[i + 1][1]].as_long()
                b0, b1 = m[s[i][0]].as_long(), m[s[i + 1][0]].as_long()
                ops.append('Hold' if h1 > h0 else 'Capture' if b1 < b0 else 'Release')
            print(f'  reachable in {k} steps:', ', '.join(ops))
            return
    print(f'  none within {bound} steps')

explore('twin', lambda bal, held, n: n <= bal)
explore('good', lambda bal, held, n: n <= bal - held)

call.prompt: Run the step query and a bounded search on the twin, whose `Hold(n)` requires only `n ≤ bal`. What is the verdict for `bal ≥ 0` there?

options.text: Inductive: no step can break it.
options.why: A `Capture` still breaks it from a state with `held > bal`, so the step query has a model. Inductive needs the step query to have none.

options.text: A CTI: the failing state cannot be reached, so strengthen the invariant.
options.why: On the good model that is the answer. On the twin it is not, because two `Hold`s stack past the balance and make the state reachable.

options.text: Reachable: a run from `Init` breaks it, so fix the command.
options.why: The twin checks `n ≤ bal` and ignores holds already placed. Two `Hold`s pass that check, and a `Capture` then spends more than `bal`.

blocks.after: The step query has a model on both models, with `held` above `bal` in the pre-state. The search separates them: the twin has a run of 3 steps, Hold, Hold, Capture, and the good model has none within 6 steps {{run:RUN-z3-cti-pair}}. The same query, the same shape of CTI, opposite verdicts. The cell prints a check on the pre-state and not its numbers, because Z3's model values are not canonical: a witness is checked, never matched.

choice.prompt: Take the good holds model and change one command: `Capture(n)` now also charges a fee of 1, so it sets `bal := bal − n − 1` and `held := held − n`. The invariant is `0 ≤ held ≤ bal`, and its inductive step has a model. What is the verdict?

options.text: Inductive: the guards still keep `held ≤ bal`.
options.why: The step has a model, so it is not inductive. `Capture` takes `n + 1` from `bal` but only `n` from `held`, so a state with `bal = held` ends with `held > bal`.

options.text: A CTI: strengthen the invariant with the missing fact.
options.why: The failing pre-state, `bal = held = 1`, is reached from `Init` by one `Hold(1)`. A reachable pre-state is not a CTI.

options.text: Reachable: a short run from `Init` breaks it, so fix `Capture`.
options.why: From `bal = 1`, `Hold(1)` and then `Capture(1)` leave `bal = −1`. Two steps from `Init` break it, so the command is the bug.

blocks.md:
A CTI is a gift: it shows which fact your invariant forgot. Here is the full procedure on the good model's CTI. You will repeat it on your own.

1. Read the pre-state. The cell checks only that `held` is above `bal`; a state such as `bal = 0`, `held = 1` has that shape.
2. Name a fact that this state breaks and that every reachable state keeps. Holds never exceed the balance: `held ≤ bal`.
3. Add it as a conjunct. The new invariant is `0 ≤ held ≤ bal`, the `I2` of S4.L4, which already implies `bal ≥ 0`.
4. Re-run three checks: `Init ⇒ Inv`, `Inv ∧ Next ⇒ Inv′`, and `Inv ⇒ Safe`, where `Safe` is the property you set out to establish, here `bal ≥ 0`.
5. Add a premise witness: a state where the invariant holds and some step is enabled. Without it, an `unsat` could be vacuous.

If a check still fails, you have a new CTI: go back to step 1.

Two cautions. Add only facts that hold in every reachable state, and read which check broke when one fails, because a wrong conjunct fails `Init ⇒ Inv` or the step. And do not edit the command to make a CTI go away: a CTI is no evidence that the command is wrong.
The three checks for `0 ≤ held ≤ bal` on the good model, plus a premise witness.
blocks.direction: Query asserts, line by line: a step from an invariant state to a state that breaks it; a start state that breaks the invariant; an invariant state that is not `Safe`; and, as the premise witness, an invariant state with a step enabled. `unsat` on the first three and `sat` on the fourth is what CL-4.4 needs.

code.text:
from z3 import *

bal, held, n, bal2, held2 = Ints('bal held n bal2 held2')
step = And(n > 0, Or(
    And(n <= bal - held, held2 == held + n, bal2 == bal),     # Hold(n)
    And(n <= held, held2 == held - n, bal2 == bal - n),       # Capture(n)
    And(n <= held, held2 == held - n, bal2 == bal)))          # Release(n)

init = And(bal >= 0, held == 0)
inv  = lambda b, h: And(0 <= h, h <= b)       # I2, the strengthened invariant
safe = lambda b, h: b >= 0                    # the property you set out to establish

def verdict(label, *claims):
    s = Solver()
    s.add(*claims)
    print(f'{label}: {s.check()}')

verdict('Inv, step, not Inv after ', inv(bal, held), step, Not(inv(bal2, held2)))
verdict('Init and not Inv         ', init, Not(inv(bal, held)))
verdict('Inv and not Safe         ', inv(bal, held), Not(safe(bal, held)))
verdict('premise: Inv and a step  ', inv(bal, held), step)

call.prompt: What does Z3 return for the first line, the inductive step for the strengthened invariant?

options.text: `sat`
options.why: `sat` expects a further CTI, but every guard now keeps `held` within `bal`, so no step escapes the invariant.

options.text: `unsat`
options.why: No state in `0 ≤ held ≤ bal` has a step that leaves it. `Hold` is guarded by the free balance, and `Capture` and `Release` are guarded by `held`.

options.text: `unknown`
options.why: Linear integer constraints of this size are decided outright. `unknown` belongs to queries like `x**y == 8` {{run:RUN-z3-unknown-pow}}.

blocks.after: The first three queries have no model and the premise witness has one {{run:RUN-z3-inductive}}. So the invariant is inductive for this command set, and the step can run from an invariant state, so the `unsat` is not vacuous. That is CL-4.4, stamped PROVED [P] · Z3 5.3.1 unsat · uncertified. It says what Z3 decided about this encoding and nothing about the encoding itself.

choice.prompt: A merchant account takes `Pay(n)` from a customer and gives `Refund(n)` back. The state is `cust`, `merch` and `paid`, which is what the merchant holds for this order. `Pay(n)` requires `n ≤ cust` and moves `n` into `merch` and `paid`. `Refund(n)` requires `n ≤ paid` and moves `n` from `merch` back to `cust`, lowering `paid`. It starts with `merch = 0`, `paid = 0` and `cust ≥ 0`. The invariant `merch ≥ 0` has a CTI at `merch = 0`, `paid = 1`. Which conjunct, added to `merch ≥ 0`, makes it inductive?

options.text: `paid ≥ 0`
options.why: The CTI has `paid = 1`, which satisfies it, so the same `Refund` still breaks `merch ≥ 0`.

options.text: `paid ≤ merch`
options.why: `Refund` needs `n ≤ paid`, and `paid ≤ merch` gives `merch − n ≥ 0`. `Pay` and `Refund` move both by the same amount, so the fact is kept.

options.text: `paid = 0`
options.why: It excludes the CTI, but `Pay(n)` makes `paid = n`. A fact that a step breaks is too strong to be inductive.

options.text: `cust ≥ 0`
options.why: It is true in every reachable state, and even inductive by itself, but it says nothing about `paid` and `merch`. The CTI survives.

blocks.md:
Sometimes the missing facts do not come: the model has more moving parts, or each new CTI shows something different. You still have to write down what you know.

CL-4.4 needs an inductive step with no model. When you do not have one, CL-4.5 is the claim: the invariant holds on every run of up to N steps. Its stamp is MODEL-CHECKED [M] with the bound and "partial", and it carries an open defeater, inductiveness [?], with the CTI listed. It is never PROVED [P], because nothing was shown about step N + 1. A bounded verdict that does not print its bound is not a claim at all.

A claim can also be worded to look stronger than it is. CL-4.5 with the CTI line deleted does that, because the CTI is the reason the claim is not [P].

The cell holds a model with two holds on one account, each with its own `Hold`, `Capture` and `Release`. The property is `bal ≥ 0`, and `inv` is yours to strengthen. Run it as written first. The state Z3 prints for a failing step names a fact that `inv` forgot, and three facts are missing, not one.[^1]

[^1]: Drawer D-18 covers the same situation for Apalache: its inductive check earns [M], never [P] on its own.
Two holds on one account. Edit `inv`, run again, and read which check changes.
blocks.direction: Query asserts: the three checks for `inv`, then, for each k up to 6, a run of k steps from `Init` that ends with `bal < 0`. `sat` on the second check is a CTI. `sat` on a search line is a trace.

code.text:
from z3 import *

def inv(bal, h1, h2):
    return And(bal >= 0)             # the invariant; add conjuncts here to strengthen it

def step(s, t, n):
    (bal, h1, h2), (bal2, h1b, h2b) = s, t
    free = bal - h1 - h2
    return And(n > 0, Or(
        And(n <= free, h1b == h1 + n, h2b == h2, bal2 == bal),           # Hold on slot 1
        And(n <= free, h2b == h2 + n, h1b == h1, bal2 == bal),           # Hold on slot 2
        And(n <= h1, h1b == h1 - n, h2b == h2, bal2 == bal - n),         # Capture slot 1
        And(n <= h2, h2b == h2 - n, h1b == h1, bal2 == bal - n),         # Capture slot 2
        And(n <= h1, h1b == h1 - n, h2b == h2, bal2 == bal),             # Release slot 1
        And(n <= h2, h2b == h2 - n, h1b == h1, bal2 == bal)))            # Release slot 2

def fresh(i):
    return Int(f'bal{i}'), Int(f'h1_{i}'), Int(f'h2_{i}')

# The three checks: Init => Inv, Inv and a step => Inv after, and Inv => Safe.
s0, s1, n = fresh(0), fresh(1), Int('n')
init = And(s0[0] >= 0, s0[1] == 0, s0[2] == 0)
checks = [
    ('Init and not Inv', [init, Not(inv(*s0))]),
    ('Inv, step, not Inv after', [inv(*s0), step(s0, s1, n), Not(inv(*s1))]),
    ('Inv and not Safe', [inv(*s0), Not(s0[0] >= 0)])]
for label, claims in checks:
    q = Solver()
    q.add(*claims)
    r = q.check()
    print(f'{label:26}', r)
    if r == sat:                     # read the state in the model: which fact does it break?
        m = q.model()
        print('   state:', {str(v): m.eval(v, model_completion=True).as_long() for v in s0})

# Bounded search from Init: a run of k steps that ends with bal < 0.
bound = 6
for k in range(bound + 1):
    s = [fresh(i) for i in range(k + 1)]
    q = Solver()
    q.add(s[0][0] >= 0, s[0][1] == 0, s[0][2] == 0)
    for i in range(k):
        q.add(step(s[i], s[i + 1], Int(f'n{i}')))
    q.add(s[k][0] < 0)
    if q.check() == sat:
        print('reachable in', k, 'steps')
        break
else:
    print('none within', bound, 'steps')

call.prompt: On the two-hold model the invariant `bal ≥ 0` has a failing step, and a search to 6 steps finds no violation. Which claim does that evidence support?

options.text: CL-4.4, PROVED [P]: the invariant is inductive.
options.why: CL-4.4 needs an inductive step with no model, and this one has a model.

options.text: CL-4.5, MODEL-CHECKED [M] · bound 6 · partial, with the CTI listed as the open defeater.
options.why: The search covers every run of up to 6 steps and no more, and the inductiveness [?] stays open because the CTI is still there.

options.text: CL-4.5 with the CTI line deleted.
options.why: Deleting the line hides the only reason the claim is not [P].

blocks.after: As written, the step has a model and the search comes back empty, so you hold a CTI and the line "none within 6 steps" {{run:RUN-z3-cti-pair}}. That is the evidence for CL-4.5 and it supports nothing stronger. If you find the three missing facts, the second check changes and the claim you can mint changes with it. The bound stays printed either way.

choice.prompt: For another invariant, `Init` implies it and the inductive step has a model. A bounded search to 4 steps finds a run of 3 steps that ends with the invariant broken, and the interpreter replays it. Which claim do you mint?

options.text: CL-4.4, PROVED [P].
options.why: CL-4.4 needs an inductive step with no model, and a replayed run shows the invariant is false, not merely not inductive.

options.text: CL-4.5, MODEL-CHECKED [M] · bound 4 · partial.
options.why: CL-4.5 says no violation was found within 4 steps, and one was. The search did not come back empty.

options.text: Neither: REFUTED [R] with 3 steps, and the command needs a fix.
options.why: A trace that replays is a witness. The invariant is broken on a real run, so no claim about it can be minted, and the fix goes in the command.

choice.prompt: On the good holds model, `Init` sets `held = 0` and `bal ≥ 0`. The invariant is `held ≤ bal`, which never mentions `bal ≥ 0`. What is the verdict?

options.text: Inductive.
options.why: `Hold` is guarded by `n ≤ bal − held`, `Capture` lowers both by `n`, and `Release` only lowers `held`. No step can break it.

options.text: A CTI: it needs `bal ≥ 0` added.
options.why: A CTI needs a step that breaks the invariant, and none does. Whether it also implies `bal ≥ 0` is a different question, the `Safe` check.

options.text: Reachable: a short run from `Init` breaks it.
options.why: Every command keeps `held ≤ bal`, so no run of any length breaks it.

choice.prompt: On the same model the invariant is `bal ≥ 0 ∧ held ≥ 0`. What is the verdict?

options.text: Inductive: both conjuncts are non-negative facts, so no step can break them.
options.why: A `Capture` from `bal = 0`, `held = 1` leaves `bal = −1`. The state satisfies both conjuncts, so the extra conjunct adds nothing against this CTI.

options.text: A CTI: strengthen it with `held ≤ bal`.
options.why: The step has a model, but `Hold` keeps `held ≤ bal` on every run from `Init`, so no run reaches it. The missing fact is `held ≤ bal`.

options.text: Reachable: fix `Capture`.
options.why: The failing state has `held > bal`, and no run from `Init` makes `held` exceed `bal` on this model.

choice.prompt: Now `Release(n)` checks only `n ≤ bal`, and not `n ≤ held`. `Hold` and `Capture` are as in the good model. The invariant is `held ≥ 0`. What is the verdict?

options.text: Inductive.
options.why: `Release` can lower `held` below zero whenever `n` exceeds `held`, so a step breaks it.

options.text: A CTI: strengthen it.
options.why: The failing pre-state can be `held = 0` with `bal ≥ 1`, which is an `Init` state, reached in zero steps. A reachable pre-state is not a CTI.

options.text: Reachable: one `Release(1)` from an `Init` state with `bal ≥ 1` breaks it.
options.why: A single step from `Init` leaves `held = −1`. The command is the bug, so `Release` gets the guard `n ≤ held`.

blocks.title: A production twin
blocks.md: TigerBeetle rejects a debit under its flag `debits_must_not_exceed_credits` when `debits_pending + debits_posted + amount` would exceed `credits_posted`. Its two-phase transfers reserve the pending amount, so a later post or void cannot break the balance invariant. Docs read 2026-10-23; pin {{run:RUN-twin-pins}}. Tracing question: which conjunct of `0 ≤ held ≤ bal` does the flag enforce at reservation, and which `Hold` guard does it use?

A pin is the commit a ref pointed to when ls-remote read it; read_at is that instant. The record is stale 60 days after its started_at and is refreshed by re-running the commands in argv.

git ls-remote was first run with several ref patterns per command (HEAD plus refs/tags/... or refs/heads/...); for leanprover/lean4 and postgres/postgres that printed nothing with exit 0. The recorded run uses one pattern per command; the pin for lean4 tags and PR 14577 uses a trailing * pattern, and every matching ref is kept in refs.

refs/pull/14577/merge is not advertised; only refs/pull/14577/head is. The v4.35.0 tag points at eb6cafb7290e8bd5f2937522d8d804f58f02bafc, the commit the bench image's Lean prints in its version string.

Twin cards that name no git repository are not pinned here: Stripe's "Idempotent requests" API page, the Zanzibar paper (USENIX ATC 2019), Jepsen's PostgreSQL 12.3 analysis, the arXiv papers on Cedar and CCF, SymCert (FMCAD 2026) and the AWS Automated Reasoning checks pages. Each card states its own read date.
